subject: Post-demo: Hosted evaluation — access playbook & next actions
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@novaretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Oct 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Hosted evaluation — access playbook & next actions

Hi Priya / Alex,

Thanks again for the time today — great to see the NovaRetail team walk through the merchandising use case. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Demo takeaway: NovaRetail prefers a hosted-first evaluation to validate response quality and latency before committing to a Dedicated pool.
- Primary metrics you mentioned: 95th pct latency <= 300ms for single-turn product description calls; peak concurrency ~120 QPS during campaigns; token-average ~45 tokens per request.
- Constraints: data residency in us-east, SOC 2 evidence requested by security, and a need to understand burst capacity for Black Friday-like spikes.

Can you confirm the concurrency numbers above and whether the 45-token average is stable across endpoints (search/rerank vs product copy)? Once confirmed we’ll propose an endpoints matrix and an initial quickstart blueprint (sandbox endpoints + traffic profile) — recommended duration: 2 weeks.

Next steps (proposal):
1) We provide a hosted quickstart playbook (endpoints, prefix caching recommendations, recommended batching and per-endpoint rate caps).
2) NovaRetail provides a small sample of production traffic (anonymized) or a representative workload to validate latency/cost estimates.
3) Schedule a 30-minute ops preflight next Wednesday (Oct 11) to review rate limits, regional endpoints, and canary routing.

I’m attaching a short playbook draft separately (internal draft) — Marissa / Karthik, feel free to amend before I send to Priya.

Thanks,
Jonas
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

---
Attachment stubs:
- Hosted-Quickstart-Playbook.pdf (summary: endpoints, canary plan, throttling guidance)
- NovaRetail-MAP.xlsx (traffic profile template)
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@novaretail.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@novaretail.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Oct 2028 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hosted evaluation — access playbook & next actions

Jonas — thanks, this is helpful. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Concurrency: our peak during a normal week is ~35 QPS; marketing campaign spikes to ~150 QPS for short bursts (2–3 hours). We can provide a sanitized traffic sample (logs) — will check with infra on timeline.
- Token average: 45 is accurate for product copy; our search/rerank calls average ~18 tokens.
- Residency: us-east required for production, but staging can be in us-west.
- Security: we will need SOC 2 Type II report and an initial penetration testing checklist before we spin up anything in a sandbox that touches PII. (We will redact PII in the traffic sample.)

Questions we have for Redwood: 
1) What per-endpoint rate limits do you recommend for hosted sandbox vs production?
2) Can Redwood handle short bursts to 150 QPS without manual capacity changes (auto-burst)?
3) What are the regional endpoint hostnames we should use for us-east vs us-west?

If you can propose the sandbox endpoints + a default per-endpoint rate cap and the quickstart playbook by Tuesday EOD (Oct 10), that would be perfect. We can then sync on Oct 11 for the preflight.

—Priya
VP Product Ops | NovaRetail
priya.shah@novaretail.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Oct 2028 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: Hosted evaluation — access playbook & next actions

Jonas / Karthik — forwarding Priya’s reply. My suggested answers and a short ops playbook to attach:

- Recommended per-endpoint rate caps (prod / sandbox):
  - product-copy endpoint: prod 600 requests/min (10 rps sustained), sandbox 300 req/min;
  - search/rerank endpoint: prod 4,800 requests/min (80 rps), sandbox 1,200 req/min (20 rps).
  - note: these are per-endpoint per-region defaults — we can tune once we ingest the sample.

- Burst handling: hosted supports automatic short-term bursting via reserved burst pools for customers on trials up to 2x sustained with short (<=3 hour) episodic allowance. For campaign-level sustained increases we recommend a short-term Dedicated burst reservation (we can provide a pricing estimate).

- Regional endpoints (vhost):
  - us-east-1.api.redwood-inference.com
  - us-west-2.api.redwood-inference.com

I attached a trimmed playbook and a MAP template for NovaRetail to fill. Proposed plan: I’ll review the playbook with Jonas, send the finalized playbook to Priya tonight, propose Oct 11 10:00am PT for the preflight, and draft a canary routing policy that starts 5% of traffic in sandbox endpoints.

Jonas — I left placeholder numbers in the playbook (Hosted-Quickstart-Playbook.pdf). If you want, I can also include a short SOC 2 evidence checklist for their security team.

Marissa
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

---
Attachment stubs:
- Hosted-Quickstart-Playbook.pdf (attached: recommended caps + canary routing + cache prefix suggestions)
- NovaRetail-MAP.xlsx (traffic sample template for NovaRetail)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@novaretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Oct 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hosted evaluation — access playbook & next actions

Hi Priya — thanks for the quick confirmations. Attached is our finalized quickstart playbook (condensed) and the MAP template. Highlights and actions below: 

1) Sandbox endpoints and hosts (staging):
   - https://us-west-2.api.redwood-inference.com/nova-retail/sandbox/product-copy
   - https://us-west-2.api.redwood-inference.com/nova-retail/sandbox/search-rerank

2) Default rate caps we’ll apply to the sandbox (modifiable after first 48h):
   - product-copy: 300 req/min (5 rps)
   - search/rerank: 1,200 req/min (20 rps)

3) Burst policy: we’ll enable auto-burst up to 2x sustained for short spikes (<=3 hours). For campaign windows that exceed the burst envelope we’ll provide a one-week Dedicated burst quote (I can loop in sales ops once you confirm campaign windows).

4) Security artifacts: Marissa attached a short SOC 2 evidence checklist. I’ve included a link to our portal where you can pull the formal report once your security team confirms access (we’ll request a signed NDA for the report).

5) Preflight call: propose Oct 11 at 10:00am PT — agenda: rate caps, sample upload, canary routing, and success criteria for the 2-week quickstart.

Please reply to confirm the preflight slot and whether you’ll share a sanitized log sample before the call (upload instructions are in the playbook).

Best,
Jonas
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
